classification.difficultyReason: Select taught rhombus diagonal and angle-bisector facts, link with triangle/straight/co-interior angles and recognise equal radii plus parallel pairs; the stem explicitly supplies the intended property family.

content.prompt: Use the properties of a rhombus to find the values of $x$, $\alpha$, $\beta$, $\gamma$ and $\theta$ in the diagrams below, giving reasons.

spec.description: Rhombus PMNO with perpendicular red dashed diagonals meeting at T, source parallel arrows, double side ticks and all unknown angle labels.
spec.mathematics: The given 65-degree angle is MPN; alpha is PTM, beta is PMT, gamma is NPO and theta is MON.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens and unknown labels appear.

answer.worked:
The diagonals of rhombus $PMNO$ meet at right angles, so $\alpha=90^\circ$.

In $\triangle PMT$,
$$\begin{align*}\beta&=180^\circ-90^\circ-65^\circ\\\beta&=25^\circ.\end{align*}$$
The diagonal $PN$ bisects the angle at $P$, so $\gamma=65^\circ$.

Since $PM\parallel ON$, alternate angles give $\theta=\beta=25^\circ$.

spec.description: Rhombus ABCD, red dashed diagonals, DC extended beyond C, exterior 70-degree angle, alpha at DCA and beta at ABD.
spec.mathematics: Opposite sides are marked parallel; AD and DC have matching double ticks.

answer.worked:
Angles on the straight line at $C$ give
$$\begin{align*}\angle DCB&=180^\circ-70^\circ\\\angle DCB&=110^\circ.\end{align*}$$
Diagonal $AC$ bisects the interior angle at $C$, so
$$\alpha=110^\circ\div2=55^\circ.$$
Co-interior angles on $AB\parallel DC$ give
$$\angle ABC=180^\circ-110^\circ=70^\circ.$$
Diagonal $BD$ bisects the interior angle at $B$, so
$$\beta=70^\circ\div2=35^\circ.$$

children.label: c
children.prompt: (The point $O$ is the centre of the circle.)

spec.description: Unfilled circle centred at O with A and C on its circumference; parallelogram OABC, OA labelled 10 cm, BC labelled x, red dashed OB, given angle ABO of 20 degrees and unknown interior angle OCB.
spec.mathematics: OA and BC have matching single parallel arrows; AB and OC have matching double arrows. Equal radii OA and OC establish a rhombus.
spec.answerVisibility: The equality of radii and all calculated values remain answer content.

answer.short:
$x=10\text{ cm}$, $\theta=140^\circ$.

Equal radii give adjacent equal sides in parallelogram $OABC$, so it is a rhombus.
answer.worked:
$OA=OC$ because both are radii of the circle. The parallel markings show that $OABC$ is a parallelogram. Its adjacent equal sides make it a rhombus, so all four sides are equal and $x=10\text{ cm}$.

Diagonal $OB$ bisects the angle at $B$, so
$$\angle ABC=2\times20^\circ=40^\circ.$$
Since $AB\parallel OC$, co-interior angles give
$$\begin{align*}\theta&=180^\circ-40^\circ\\\theta&=140^\circ.\end{align*}$$
